History

The drying rack is a hanging tower of mesh tiers that holds plant material in the air so it can dry evenly, and it descends from the herb-drying frames and net bags that gardeners have used for centuries. The modern form is a collapsible cylinder of polyester mesh over a flexible steel wireframe, with zippered chambers stacked one above another and a hook at the top so the whole tower hangs from a bar. The standard example in this record is the six-tier rack, 600 millimetres across and 1,194 millimetres long when hanging, with each chamber 171 millimetres high; a four-tier version, 457 millimetres across, fits a 2 by 2 tent, and eight-tier versions reach 1,700 millimetres. The rack collapses flat into a carry bag when the season is over, and it springs open from the bag in seconds. The record here describes the rack as a product — its tiers, its mesh, its frame, its hook — and it does not tell anyone how to dry any particular plant or how long any drying or curing should take. The sources cited at the end of this record give the reader places to check each stage of that change.

The supply in detail

The Drying Rack works by material is spread in a single layer on each mesh tier; air passes through the mesh floor and walls; the tower hangs from one hook so air moves around it on all sides It is made from non-toxic polyester mesh; flexible steel wireframe; steel hanging hook; zippered chambers; carry bag, and a common example measures 6 tiers; 600 mm (24 in) diameter; 1,194 mm (47 in) hanging length; each chamber 171 mm (6.75 in) high. The parts fit together in a fixed order, and each part has one job: to hold the material, to apply the mechanism, or to carry the result to the user. Because the parts are simple and the mechanism is mechanical or thermal rather than electronic in its basic form, the supply can be understood by inspection, measured with a ruler, and checked by the arithmetic in this record. The variants listed in the specification show how makers change size, material, and detail while keeping the same working principle, and the scale variants at the end of this record show the same design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes.

Parts and variants

Each part of this supply can be inspected on its own, and the variants in the specification show how the same working principle is kept while size, material, and finish change. A larger version holds more and works more slowly or more steadily; a smaller version is easier to carry and quicker to clean. Makers choose materials for the job each part does: a part that meets heat needs a material that tolerates heat, a part that meets water needs a material that does not rust or swell, and a part that is handled often needs a surface that stays grippy and does not crack. The scale variants at the end of this record carry that same logic further, showing the design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes, so the reader can see which dimensions change with scale and which stay the same.

Spec

Materials: Non-toxic polyester mesh; flexible steel wireframe; steel hanging hook; zippered chambers; carry bag

Dimensions: 6 tiers; 600 mm (24 in) diameter; 1,194 mm (47 in) hanging length; each chamber 171 mm (6.75 in) high

Mechanism: Material is spread in a single layer on each mesh tier; air passes through the mesh floor and walls; the tower hangs from one hook so air moves around it on all sides

Use: Hang the rack from a bar or hook, open the zipper of a tier, spread material in a single layer, close the zipper, repeat for the other tiers

Care: Empty each tier after use; brush off loose material; wash the mesh gently and dry fully; collapse flat into the carry bag for storage

Variants: 2, 4, 6, and 8 tiers; 457 mm (18 in), 600 mm (24 in), 800 mm (32 in), and 900 mm (36 in) diameters; removable tiers; with carry bag

Materials and design

A drying rack is a tower of mesh and wire, and its design is a balance between holding a load and folding flat. The mesh is non-toxic polyester, chosen because it is breathable, washable, and strong enough to hold material without stretching, and because it lets air pass through the floor of each tier as well as around the sides. The frame is flexible steel wire, chosen because it holds each disc open under load and still folds flat into a carry bag when the season is over; the sources describe the wire as rust-proof and high-tensile.

Build it yourself

A drying rack is a genuine woodworking and sewing build, and it can be made from dowels, mesh, and cord. Cut six discs of polyester mesh 600 millimetres across, and cut six wooden rings from 12 millimetre dowel bent into circles 600 millimetres across, or use ready-made embroidery hoops of the same size as the rings. Sew each mesh disc to its ring with a whip stitch around the full circle, pulling the mesh taut so it does not sag in the middle. Cut three lengths of cord 1,400 millimetres long, and tie them to the rings at three points spaced evenly around the circle, spacing the rings 171 millimetres apart along the cords so the chambers match the standard rack.

3D printing

A drying rack itself is not 3D-printable: its tiers are polyester mesh and its frame is steel wire, and no home printer prints mesh or wire, so a printed rack would be a solid plastic disc with no airflow and would not dry anything. This record says so plainly and gives directions for printable accessories instead: tier clips and a hook adapter. Print the tier clips in PETG, which is tough and survives being handled with wet hands: use a 0.4 millimetre nozzle, 0.2 millimetre layer height, 3 walls, and 30 percent gyroid infill, printed flat on the bed with no supports. The clips are C-shaped, 50 millimetres long, and snap over the wireframe ring to hold a label tag or to join two tiers together.

Use and program

A drying rack is used by hanging it and filling its tiers. Hang the rack from a bar or hook, open the zipper of a tier, spread material in a single layer on the mesh, close the zipper, and repeat for the other tiers; the tower then hangs clear of the floor with air moving around it on all sides and through the mesh floors. The program in this record computes the numbers behind that use: the area of one 600 millimetre tier, the total area across all six tiers, the volume of one chamber at 171 millimetres high, the total volume of the tower, and the load capacity per tier from the stated 3 kilogram total.

Science proof

A drying rack works by giving air access to material from every direction at once. Each tier is a flat disc of open mesh, so air passes through the floor of the chamber as well as around its sides, and the material is spread in a single layer instead of piled in a heap where the middle stays damp. The mesh is non-toxic polyester, chosen because it is breathable, washable, and strong enough to hold a load without stretching, and the frame is flexible steel wire, chosen because it holds the disc open under load and still folds flat for storage. The numbers show the scale: one tier of the six-tier rack is 600 millimetres across, giving about 0.28 square metres of drying area per tier and about 1.70 square metres across all six, with each chamber about 171 millimetres high and about 48 litres of space.

Math proof

The demo computes the supply from its own specification, using the formula A = pi * (d/2)^2, where A is one tier area in square millimetres; d is the tier diameter in millimetres. The key figures are tiers = 6, diameter_mm = 600.0, chamber_height_mm = 171.0, hanging_length_mm = 1194.0, capacity_kg = 3.0. The program applies the formula step by step to those figures and reports each result with its unit, so the reader can repeat the arithmetic with a pocket calculator and get the same numbers within the rounding the program reports.

Use and care

Hang the rack from a bar or hook, open the zipper of a tier, spread material in a single layer, close the zipper, repeat for the other tiers Empty each tier after use; brush off loose material; wash the mesh gently and dry fully; collapse flat into the carry bag for storage Keep the supply dry when it is stored, keep its working surfaces clean, and replace worn parts when they no longer do their job.

Legal note

Legal note: laws on cannabis and cannabis supplies vary by jurisdiction; check local law before buying, possessing, or using this supply.

  • Happy Hydro — AC Infinity 4-Tier Drying Rack — https://happyhydro.com/products/ac-infinity-18-inch-durable-polyester-herb-drying-rack — The 4-tier rack is a collapsible drying rack with durable polyester mesh and a steel wireframe; diameter 18 in (45.7 cm), length 31 in (78.7 cm), 4 chambers; it fits 2x2 or larger grow tents and includes a hanging hook and carrying bag.

"""Demo: drying rack — The Drying Rack."""
import hashlib, math
def compute():
    tiers = 6; d_mm = 600.0; chamber_h = 171.0; length_mm = 1194.0; capacity_kg = 3.0
    tier_area = math.pi * (d_mm / 2.0) ** 2 / 1000000.0
    total_area = tier_area * tiers
    tier_vol = tier_area * (chamber_h / 1000.0) * 1000.0
    total_vol = tier_vol * tiers
    per_tier_kg = capacity_kg / tiers
    return {"tiers": tiers, "diameter_mm": d_mm, "chamber_height_mm": chamber_h, "hanging_length_mm": length_mm, "tier_area_m2": round(tier_area, 4), "total_area_m2": round(total_area, 3), "tier_volume_L": round(tier_vol, 1), "total_volume_L": round(total_vol, 1), "capacity_kg": capacity_kg, "per_tier_kg": round(per_tier_kg, 2)}
def main():
    a = compute(); b = compute()
    sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    print(f"tiers: {a['tiers']}")
    print(f"diameter_mm: {a['diameter_mm']}")
    print(f"chamber_height_mm: {a['chamber_height_mm']}")
    print(f"hanging_length_mm: {a['hanging_length_mm']}")
    print(f"tier_area_m2: {a['tier_area_m2']}")
    print(f"total_area_m2: {a['total_area_m2']}")
    print(f"tier_volume_L: {a['tier_volume_L']}")
    print(f"total_volume_L: {a['total_volume_L']}")
    print(f"capacity_kg: {a['capacity_kg']}")
    print(f"per_tier_kg: {a['per_tier_kg']}")
    print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
    print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
    print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The clips are C-shaped, 50 millimetres long, and snap over the wireframe ring to hold a label tag or to join two tiers together. """The Drying Rack — full working program.

Computes the same quantities as the record demo (drying rack),
as a documented module with a class and a run() method.
Run: python3 program.py
"""
import hashlib
import math


class SupplyCalculator:
    """Calculator for The Drying Rack."""

    def compute(self):
        """Return the computed quantities as a dict."""
        tiers = 6; d_mm = 600.0; chamber_h = 171.0; length_mm = 1194.0; capacity_kg = 3.0
        tier_area = math.pi * (d_mm / 2.0) ** 2 / 1000000.0
        total_area = tier_area * tiers
        tier_vol = tier_area * (chamber_h / 1000.0) * 1000.0
        total_vol = tier_vol * tiers
        per_tier_kg = capacity_kg / tiers
        return {"tiers": tiers, "diameter_mm": d_mm, "chamber_height_mm": chamber_h, "hanging_length_mm": length_mm, "tier_area_m2": round(tier_area, 4), "total_area_m2": round(total_area, 3), "tier_volume_L": round(tier_vol, 1), "total_volume_L": round(total_vol, 1), "capacity_kg": capacity_kg, "per_tier_kg": round(per_tier_kg, 2)}

    def run(self):
        """Compute twice, print named results and SHA-256 digests."""
        a = self.compute()
        b = self.compute()
        sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        for key in sorted(a):
            print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
        print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
        print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
        print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
        return a


if __name__ == "__main__":
    SupplyCalculator().run()
